newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq buys 80-85,000 tonnes U.S. wheat - traders.
newsitem.headline: Iraq buys 80-85,000 tonnes U.S. wheat - traders.

text.p: Iraq on Tuesday bought between 80 and 85,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for October shipment and an unspecified tonnage of Australian wheat, European grain traders said.

Iraq bought one cargo of 30-35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat at $186.75 per tonne, cost and freight, for delivery to Umm Qasr and another 50,000 tonnes at $220.20 per tonne for delivery by truck from Jordan's port of Aqaba.
Exporters said it was not immediately clear if that cargo was for delivery to Baghdad or other parts of Iraq.

Exporters also said Iraq had bought some wheat from Australia, but had no further details. "It is certain they bought from Australia but we will never exactly know the price nor the tonnage," one exporter said.
Iraq bought the U.S. and Australian wheat under a U.N.-monitored oil-for-food deal. One exporter also said Iraq was expected to also buy some Canadian wheat.

Negotiations between Iraqi officials and exporters were still going on for the purchase of some 100,000 tonnes of French wheat for shipment in September and October, with quality criteria being the main focus. Exporters said they were awaiting an answer from Iraq later today or tomorrow.
